title.value: Build an exam-marking app for a hackathon

introduction.value: The poster built a mobile web app that scans exam papers and marks them with AI using Replit Agent, winning $10,000 for about $15 in credits over 22 hours.

method.value: The poster used Replit Agent to build a mobile web app in a 24-hour hackathon. The app used the phone camera to capture exam papers, uploaded images to a server, sent them to the OpenAI API for vision-based reading, and returned grades as JSON; the poster says they repeatedly had the agent add comments and console logs, then manually debugged logic and data-flow issues when the agent stalled.

outcome.value: They say the project won the hackathon and brought in $10,000. It took 22 of the 24 hours, and a major failure point was AI-generated logic that put steps in the wrong order, costing about six hours of debugging.

notes.value: Their reported cost was about $15 in Replit credits, but they stress that after a few failed fixes you may need to inspect the code and re-plan the flow yourself.

source_text.body:
Build an exam-marking app for a hackathon
The poster built a mobile web app that scans exam papers and marks them with AI using Replit Agent, winning $10,000 for about $15 in credits over 22 hours.
Done with
RA
Replit Agent
What they did
The poster used Replit Agent to build a mobile web app in a 24-hour hackathon. The app used the phone camera to capture exam papers, uploaded images to a server, sent them to the OpenAI API for vision-based reading, and returned grades as JSON; the poster says they repeatedly had the agent add comments and console logs, then manually debugged logic and data-flow issues when the agent stalled.
How it went
They say the project won the hackathon and brought in $10,000. It took 22 of the 24 hours, and a major failure point was AI-generated logic that put steps in the wrong order, costing about six hours of debugging.
Worth knowing
Their reported cost was about $15 in Replit credits, but they stress that after a few failed fixes you may need to inspect the code and re-plan the flow yourself.
Try it yourself
with
Replit Agent
Copy prompt
Build a mobile-friendly web app that lets me [scan/upload] [type of document, e.g. exam papers] with my phone camera and uses AI to [mark/grade/summarize] them against [answer key or rubric]. Finish when I can upload a sample document and see a score with a short explanation for each answer. Ask me before you publish it or connect any paid API keys.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/replit/comments/1jf3kja/won_my_first_hackathon_with_the_replit_agent_v2
